big_idea: Shoppers IDENTIFY money and COMPARE values to buy and sell.
learning_intention: We are learning to identify and compare Canadian money.
student_learning_goal: I can identify and compare Canadian money.
success_criteria: I can BUY an item with the right money.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Penny + Cassie — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Penny + Cassie: Today's BIG MARKET — name money, compare, and BUY! Penny opens the unit refrain: 'COUNT the VALUE, not the COINS!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Penny and Cassie puppets in capes. 'Shoppers — today is our BIG MARKET! We use ALL we know: 6 coins, 4 bills, compare values, and BUY items!'

Review the 4 shopper steps:
- Step 1 — IDENTIFY coins.
- Step 2 — IDENTIFY bills.
- Step 3 — COMPARE values.
- Step 4 — BUY (match money to price).

Demo briefly:
- Hold a quarter. Class: 'QUARTER, 25¢!'
- Hold a $10 bill. Class: 'TEN DOLLARS, purple!'
- Compare: $5 vs $10. 'TEN MORE!'
- Buy: apple = $1. 'I pay 1 LOONIE!'

'Penny + Cassie say — shoppers IDENTIFY money and COMPARE!'

Now show the 4 stations:
- Station 1: COINS — name 4 coins.
- Station 2: BILLS — name 4 bills.
- Station 3: COMPARE — 4 pairs.
- Station 4: BUY — pay for 2 items.

Each child rotates 5 min per station and records on TEMPLATE.

'Penny + Cassie say — be a SUPER SHOPPER!'

steps.instruction: Hand out templates. 4 stations rotation (~5 min each).
Stretch: write a 'shopper's brag' — one sentence per station.
Help at Station 4 with paying — 'use loonie for $1, fiver for $5'.

STRATEGY COMPARE: At the consolidation, two children share different payments for the same item — Penny used 1 toonie, Cassie used 2 loonies, both paid $2. Sentence frame: 'Both are EQUAL because ___'. Cite Empson/CGI strategy-comparison framing on equivalent-value reasoning.
steps.teacher_prompt: Penny: 'Same price, different payment. The math says: same VALUE, different ways. Both are right.'

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Four signals: identifies coins; identifies bills; compares; buys.

consolidation.exit_routine: Closing market refrain — Penny + Cassie + class chant: 'COUNT the VALUE, not the COINS! Same VALUE, different ways!' Repeat 3x. Each child shows their winning payment to the class and explains why both Cassie's coins AND Penny's bills could have made it equal.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child OVERPAYS without realizing — repairing the no-compare-to-price trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the capstone market, Grade 1 children commonly default to physical heuristics: grab the BIGGEST coin/bill, or grab MANY small coins, regardless of price. Empson & CGI strategy-comparison work places the move from physical heuristic to value-reasoned payment as the unit's terminal target — without it, the unit's content has not transferred.

Today integrates Lessons 1-4: name (L1), value (L2), bills (L3), compare/equal-values (L4) into a market simulation where children must choose payment that EQUALS the price.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Capstone Station 4. Item costs $1. Child pays a $20 bill.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Penny asks — what's the PRICE? $1. What did you pay? $20. Is $20 EQUAL to $1?'

Probe. '$20 is MORE than $1. You'd get CHANGE BACK! Or pay just $1 — a loonie.'

Generalise. 'Penny says — pay EQUAL to price (or get change). Don't overpay!'

If still confused: line up money against price. '$1 = LOONIE. Use 1 loonie!'
common_misconceptions: Bigger bill = better. (Repair: equal is best.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child grabs ANY money: line up the price card next to ONE matching coin/bill so the quantity becomes salient. Child names the value first.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child knows price > pay but picks wrong coin: drop to value chart on Cassie's counter. Child reads value, matches.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child defaults to bills: drill the loonie-for-$1 refrain — '$1 = 1 loonie OR 4 quarters OR 10 dimes.' Cite Empson/CGI on strategy-comparison.

parts_outline.task: Pay for 2 items: choose the right money.

expected_image_assets: Item icons with prices for Part 3
